subject: Physics
posted_prompt: When a prism is placed in sunlight, white light passing through it will be broken down into a band of seven colors. Observe the distribution and order of the colors in the band.
manual: Instructions for the Experiment: Light Dispersion by a PrismI. Basic Experiment Information1. Experiment Title: Light Dispersion (Prism Light Splitting)2. Subject: Natural Science – Physics (Optics)3. Experiment Objective: To observe that white sunlight passing through a prism is dispersed into a band of seven colors, and to identify the distribution and order of these colors.II. Experimental EquipmentTriangular glass prism (one piece, clean and transparent), sunlight (direct sunlight near a window or outdoor sunlight), white screen or white paper (used to receive the spectrum), darkened room or shaded area (to improve contrast), prism stand or books (optional, for stabilizing the prism).III. Experimental ProcedurePreparation Stage: Choose a location where direct sunlight is available. Slightly darken the surrounding environment by closing curtains or turning off indoor lights to make the light band clearer. Place a white screen or white paper vertically or flat on a table.Prism Placement: Place the glass prism on a stable surface or prism stand near the sunlight source. Adjust the prism so that sunlight enters one face of the prism at an angle.Core Operation: Slowly rotate or tilt the prism until the refracted light emerging from the prism falls onto the white screen or paper.Observation: Carefully observe the light band formed on the screen. Adjust the prism angle if necessary until a clear and complete color band appears.Experiment Conclusion: Once the color band is clearly visible, fix the prism position and observe the color distribution and order. After observation, remove the prism and store the equipment properly.IV. Observation of Experimental Phenomena1. Initial State: Before the prism is placed in sunlight, the sunlight appears white and no color band is seen on the screen.2. During the Experiment: After sunlight passes through the prism, a long colored light band appears on the white screen.3. Final Observation: The light band is composed of seven distinct colors arranged in order: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. Red light deviates the least, while violet light deviates the most.V. Summary of Experimental PrincipleWhite light is composed of light of different wavelengths. When white light passes through a prism, different wavelengths are refracted by different amounts due to the prism material having different refractive indices for different colors. This causes white light to spread out into a spectrum of seven colors, a phenomenon called dispersion.VI. Experimental Precautions1. Do not look directly at the sun to avoid eye damage.2. Ensure the prism surfaces are clean to obtain a clear spectrum.3. Keep the prism stable during observation to prevent the spectrum from shaking or disappearing.
high_level_evaluation_guide: Target concept: Light dispersion by a prism. Minimum assumptions: white sunlight contains multiple wavelengths, and a transparent triangular prism refracts light. Expected phenomena storyline: (1) initial scene shows white sunlight incident on a prism; (2) light enters and exits the prism at an angle; (3) a colored band gradually appears on a white screen; (4) colors stabilize in the order red to violet, with red least deviated and violet most deviated. Visibility requirements: clear view of prism orientation, incoming sunlight, and the full spectrum on the screen; camera angle should allow simultaneous observation of prism and color band.
